uart.signal: firmware-samd21-demo brings SERCOM0 up the way a driver does — NVMCTRL wait states, the SYSCTRL.PCLKSR ready-flag poll, three GCLK SYNCBUSY spins, PM.APBCMASK, a WRCONFIG pad mux, then CTRLB before CTRLA.ENABLE — and its bytes reach the capture sink through the DRE poll. Two separate lines are asserted, so a model that sets DRE once and forgets fails: it emits one byte and then spins in putc forever.
uart.lane: core-ci: cargo test -p labwired-core --test strict_onboarding (the gate EXECUTES examples/samd21-smoke/io-smoke.yaml through the CLI and fails the board if any assertion fails)

spi.gap: SERCOM is one block that becomes a UART, an SPI controller or an I2C controller depending on CTRLA.MODE. Only USART mode is modelled; a SERCOM put into SPI mode goes inert rather than answering an SPI driver out of a USART register map.

i2c.gap: Same block, same gap as SPI: SERCOM I2CM/I2CS modes are not modelled.
